ledger.x: 19 CE: Gondophares declares independence in Drangiana.

c. 20 CE: Gondophares takes the Kabul valley, Punjab and Sindh. 'Gondophares became the ruler of areas comprising Arachosia, Seistan, Sindh, Punjab, and the Kabul valley', 'perhaps after the death of the important ruler Azes'; Gondophares page: he 'took over the Kabul valley and the Punjab and Sindh region area from…

c. 50 CE: the Kushans begin absorbing the north. 'From the middle of the 1st century AD the Kushans under Kujula Kadphises began absorbing the northern Indian part of the kingdom'; Hou Hanshu: Kujula 'invaded Anxi (Indo-Parthia), and took the Gaofu (Kabul) region' and 'defeated the whole of the kingdoms…

c. 90 CE: Punjab and Sindh pass to the Kushans. Cliopatria's Indian shape ends in 90; the Kushan page has Vima Takto (c. 80-127) 'expanded the Kushan Empire into the northwest of South Asia' and 'defeated Tianzhu (North-western India) and installed Generals'. No page dates the last Indo-Parthian loss.

c. 226 CE: the Sasanians take Sakastan. 'They managed to retain control of Sakastan, until its conquest by the Sasanian Empire in c. 224/5'; 'The Kingdoms of Turan and Sakastan ended when they submitted to the Sasanian ruler Ardeshir I circa 230 CE'. The infobox gives 226.

wars.name: Gondophares' conquest of the Indo-Scythian lands
wars.outcome: Gondophares 'took over the Kabul valley and the Punjab and Sindh region area from the Scythian king Azes'; Indo-Scythian vassals switched allegiance.

wars.name: Kushan absorption of the Indo-Parthian north
wars.outcome: The Kushans under Kujula Kadphises 'began absorbing the northern Indian part of the kingdom' from the middle of the 1st century; the Indo-Parthians refocused on Turan and Sakastan.

certainty.note: Known from coins, a few inscriptions and Greek and Chinese lines; no frontier is dated or surveyed.
